scenes.tts: A seed can become a huge tree while the soil hardly shrinks. What becomes the wood? Watch one tiny seed beside a growing trunk. The tree gains layer after layer. The soil gauge barely moves. Something outside the soil must supply most of that new material.
scenes.visual: Colour map for the entire film: gold means light energy, teal means carbon dioxide, blue means water, green means sugar, and brown means wood. Fill the frame with one seed, one growing tree and a wide soil-mass gauge. The tree grows upward while the soil gauge changes only slightly. Mark the size change 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: A seed can become a huge tree while the soil hardly shrinks. What becomes the wood? Watch one tiny seed beside a growing trunk. The tree gains layer after layer. The soil gauge barely moves. Something outside the soil must supply most of that new material.

scenes.visual: Brief title over the same living tree world: 'What Becomes a Tree?' Keep branches swaying and water drifting upward. Do not cut to an empty title card.

scenes.tts: Start by sorting matter from energy. Matter has mass and can become part of the tree. Energy can move or change form, but it does not become wood. Sunlight reaches the leaf as radiant energy. It powers the building, the way electricity runs a factory's machines without becoming part of the product.
scenes.visual: Keep the tree centred. Slide teal and blue blocks onto a tray labelled MATTER. Send a gold pulse along a separate thin wire labelled ENERGY to a small machine icon beside the tray. The machine runs and the matter tray gains blocks, while the gold pulse never joins the blocks or the trunk.
scenes.narration: Start by sorting matter from energy. Matter has mass and can become part of the tree. Energy can move or change form, but it does not become wood. Sunlight reaches the leaf as radiant energy. It powers the building, the way electricity runs a factory's machines without becoming part of the product.

scenes.tts: Water enters through roots and moves upward. Carbon dioxide enters leaves from the air. Light arrives at those leaves too. The plant uses the light energy to build sugar from carbon dioxide and water. Oxygen leaves as another product. The word equation is a summary, not one single step.
scenes.visual: Blue water drops rise from soil through roots. Teal carbon-dioxide blocks drift through a large leaf opening. Gold light pulses land on the leaf. Inside a large labelled leaf panel, the teal and blue blocks transform into one green SUGAR block while oxygen blocks drift out. Show the word equation on screen with words only.
scenes.narration: Water enters through roots and moves upward. Carbon dioxide enters leaves from the air. Light arrives at those leaves too. The plant uses the light energy to build sugar from carbon dioxide and water. Oxygen leaves as another product. The word equation is a summary, not one single step.

scenes.tts: Now predict. Which paths carry matter that can enter the trunk? Which path carries only energy? Follow each colour before the tree grows again.
scenes.visual: Freeze the tree's growth but keep gold, teal and blue paths moving slowly. Put the two questions at the top. Let each coloured path end at a large question mark beside the trunk.
scenes.narration: Now predict. Which paths carry matter that can enter the trunk? Which path carries only energy? Follow each colour before the tree grows again.

scenes.visual: Hold the prediction questions. Keep the three coloured paths drifting gently. Do not reveal the answer.

scenes.tts: The teal carbon dioxide and blue water paths carry matter. The gold light path carries energy. Light powers sugar-building from carbon dioxide and water; conditions limit its speed. The first half explains what can become wood. The second half reminds us that building cannot always run faster.
scenes.visual: Guide teal and blue blocks into the green sugar block, then stretch the green block into a brown trunk layer. The gold pulse powers the transformation but continues along its own path. Place the exact guiding rule beside the tree, then shrink it into a small rule tab for later scenes.
scenes.narration: The teal carbon dioxide and blue water paths carry matter. The gold light path carries energy. Light powers sugar-building from carbon dioxide and water; conditions limit its speed. The first half explains what can become wood. The second half reminds us that building cannot always run faster.

scenes.tts: In plants and algae, this work happens inside chloroplasts. Chloroplasts are green parts of some cells, mostly in leaves. Chlorophyll inside them captures radiant energy. Roots, which sit in darkness, usually have no chloroplasts. Photosynthetic bacteria do the work without chloroplasts.
scenes.visual: Zoom into the same leaf without leaving the world. Enlarge one cell, then several green labelled CHLOROPLAST blocks. A gold pulse lands on a chlorophyll patch inside one block. Pan down to a root-cell inset with no chloroplast blocks, then show a separate tiny bacterium icon labelled 'no chloroplast'. No molecular structures.
scenes.narration: In plants and algae, this work happens inside chloroplasts. Chloroplasts are green parts of some cells, mostly in leaves. Chlorophyll inside them captures radiant energy. Roots, which sit in darkness, usually have no chloroplasts. Photosynthetic bacteria do the work without chloroplasts.

scenes.tts: Sugar does not have one destination. Some is used now as cells release energy for living. Some is linked into starch and stored. Some is rebuilt into wood and new leaves. Each route starts with the same green sugar block made in the leaf.
scenes.visual: Return to the whole tree. One green sugar block travels along a branching path. It powers a gently glowing cell, stacks into a labelled STARCH store in a root, and stretches into a brown trunk ring plus a new leaf. Keep all three destinations visible without adding more than six labelled objects.
scenes.narration: Sugar does not have one destination. Some is used now as cells release energy for living. Some is linked into starch and stored. Some is rebuilt into wood and new leaves. Each route starts with the same green sugar block made in the leaf.

scenes.tts: That stored chemical energy can move through a food web. A rabbit eats clover, and a fox eats the rabbit. Both depend on energy captured by a producer. Almost every food web begins this way. A few communities use chemical energy instead of light.
scenes.visual: Grow clover beside the tree. Move one green energy token from clover to a rabbit cartoon, then to a fox cartoon. Keep the gold origin line visible behind the token. Fade in a small cave-and-vent exception icon labelled 'chemical energy' without changing the main path.
scenes.narration: That stored chemical energy can move through a food web. A rabbit eats clover, and a fox eats the rabbit. Both depend on energy captured by a producer. Almost every food web begins this way. A few communities use chemical energy instead of light.

scenes.tts: Return to the tree. Its soil did not need to become the trunk. Matter arrived mainly as carbon dioxide, with water also supplying atoms. Light supplied the energy for building sugar. Light supplies the energy; carbon dioxide and water supply the matter. The plant then used that sugar to make living material and feed other life.
scenes.visual: Bring back the opening seed, full tree and soil gauge. Replay teal and blue blocks entering, a green sugar block forming, and a brown trunk ring growing. The gold pulse powers the change. End on the full tree and the separate energy and matter paths.
scenes.narration: Return to the tree. Its soil did not need to become the trunk. Matter arrived mainly as carbon dioxide, with water also supplying atoms. Light supplied the energy for building sugar. Light supplies the energy; carbon dioxide and water supply the matter. The plant then used that sugar to make living material and feed other life.

scenes.visual: One-line end card only: 'Light supplies the energy; carbon dioxide and water supply the matter.' No title, website, subtitle or smaller line. Keep a faint gold pulse moving behind the single line.
